relations.statement: For subsets O1 ⊆ O2 of the points of P, A(O1) ⊆ A(O2), where A(O) = M_{2^|O|} tensored with identity on the qubits outside O.
relations.hypotheses: O1 ⊆ O2 ⊆ points of P; one qubit per point

relations.statement: If every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then A(O1) and A(O2) commute.
relations.hypotheses: O1 and O2 are pairwise spacelike; spacelike means distinct and incomparable in P. Disjointness of O1 and O2 follows from irreflexivity.

relations.statement: Spacelike is symmetric and irreflexive but not transitive. In the N poset (0<2, 1<2, 1<3), 0~1 and 0~3 are spacelike, yet 1<3 are related.

lemmas.statement: O1 ⊆ O2 implies A(O1) ⊆ A(O2) (embedding X ↦ X ⊗ I).
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem isotony {n : ℕ} (O1 O2 : Finset (Fin n)) (h : O1 ⊆ O2) : True := by sorry

lemmas.statement: Pairwise spacelike O1, O2 gives commuting A(O1), A(O2), because the supports are disjoint and tensor factors on disjoint qubits commute.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem locality {n : ℕ} (O1 O2 : Finset (Fin n)) (h : Disjoint O1 O2) : True := by sorry

lemmas.statement: In the N poset, spacelike(0,1), spacelike(0,3), and 1<3, so spacelike is not transitive.

near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The N poset has 0~1 and 0~3 spacelike but 1<3 related, so transitivity fails (0~1 and 1~3 would be needed, which also fails).

near_misses.claim: The net encodes Haag-Kastler locality, with commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The net has no dynamics, time-slice, or covariance. The commutation is purely kinematic, from disjoint tensor supports.

open_obligations: No cited SRC declaration defines FiniteStrictPoset, the net A(O), or spacelike. All are proposed_new.
build_tensor is a 6x6 Kronecker product of a 2x2 and a 3x3 matrix, so it does not match the qubit embedding X ⊗ I. It is not cited.
The Lean skeletons are placeholders and need real statements over Matrix and the Kronecker product.
The embedding of A(O1) into A(O2) needs a formal definition, via reindexing of tensor factors.
Dynamics, time-slice and covariance are out of scope.
